newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian dam set to woo investing public.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian dam set to woo investing public.

text.p: Malaysia's $6.18-billion Bakun hydroelectric dam being built in a Borneo rainforest is preparing to list on the Malaysian stock market with the help of 54 underwriters and government backing.

The Bakun Hydro-Electric Corp Bhd (BHEC) is expected to make an initial public offering (IPO) on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange in late July or early August, lead underwriter Commerce International Bankers Bhd said on Tuesday.
On Tuesday, BHEC signed an underwriting agreement with 54 Malaysian institutions including CIMB.

The cost of the dam had been estimated at $5.5 billion, but the company has raised that to $6.18 billion (15.5 million ringgit) after taking into account interest costs during construction, BHEC said.
BHEC, the firm operating the dam, is selling 1.5 billion shares at two ringgit each to raise 3.0 billion ringgit, the biggest stock offering in the history of the Malaysian bourse.

The IPO to foreign and local investors will have 375 million shares, or 25 percent of the total stock. The other 75 percent has been allocated to state and federal agencies and to Ekran Bhd, the main contractor, which will take 32 percent.
Another three billion ringgit will come from a rights offering. The balance of the financing -- about 9.5 billion ringgit -- will come from debt issues, analysts said.
The 2,400-megawatt capacity dam would clear 69,000 hectares of forests, displace more than 9,000 tribal residents and create a reservoir the size of Singapore in Sarawak state.
It is due to be finished by 2003. Preparatory work on the project started last year. Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Tuesday the dam's diversion tunnels have been completed.
"I don't foresee any problems in implementing (the dam) in the time that has been specified," Mahathir said.
The project has been criticised by environmentalists and non-governmental organisations (NGOs) who have questioned the dam's size and whether it was even needed.
On Tuesday, Concerned NGOs on Bakun issued a statement saying it was "disappointed" the underwriting was proceeding.
"If it weren't for the strong governmental support, if the project's viability were left to the scrutiny of market forces, would Bakun be worth its initial offer price?" the group asked.
Ten percent of BHEC's shares had initially been reserved for foreign investors. But Ekran recently said Malaysian institutions would also be allowed to purchase those shares.
Mahathir has been a defender of the project, which he said he wished had been started in 1976 when it was first approved.
While stopping short of offering financial guarantees for Bakun, Mahathir called the dam a "national project", and said the government would "always be behind this project".
Analysts have said that because of the government's firm support of Bakun, the project is likely to be pushed ahead despite or criticism.

"I think once the underwriters have signed on the dotted line, whether the shares are oversubscribed or not, Bakun will go ahead," said an analyst who follows the company. "As far as risk to the company, there's really no more risk. The risk has been transferred to the underwriters."
A consortium led by ABB Asea Brown Boveri Ltd and Brazil's Companhia Brasileria Projectos o Obras (CBPO) is responsible for construction of the dam.
($1=2.51 ringgit)
